Part 1 — Text Preprocessing & Sequence Preparation¶

Clean text by removing HTML tags, special characters, and converting to lowercase¶

In [5]:
# Clean text: remove HTML, special characters, make lowercase
def clean_text(text):
    text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', text)        # remove HTML tags like <br>
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z\s]', '', text)    # keep only letters and spaces
    text = text.lower().strip()
    return text

train_texts_clean = [clean_text(t) for t in train_texts]
test_texts_clean = [clean_text(t) for t in test_texts]

print("Before cleaning:", train_texts[0][:150])
print("\nAfter cleaning:", train_texts_clean[0][:150])

Tokenize text and build a vocabulary of top 20,000 words¶

In [8]:
VOCAB_SIZE = 20000    # keep top 20,000 words
MAX_LEN = 250         # max sequence length
EMBEDDING_DIM = 100   # word vector size

# Fit tokenizer on training data only
tokenizer = Tokenizer(num_words=VOCAB_SIZE, oov_token='<OOV>')
tokenizer.fit_on_texts(train_texts_clean)

# Turn words into numbers
train_sequences = tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(train_texts_clean)
test_sequences = tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(test_texts_clean)

word_index = tokenizer.word_index
print(f"Total unique words: {len(word_index)}")
print(f"Vocabulary used: {VOCAB_SIZE}")
print(f"\nSample word-to-number mapping:")
for word, idx in list(word_index.items())[:10]:
    print(f"  '{word}' -> {idx}")

Build embedding matrix by mapping our vocabulary to GloVe vectors¶

In [13]:
# Load GloVe vectors into a dictionary
glove_embeddings = {}
with open('glove.6B.100d.txt', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    for line in f:
        parts = line.split()
        word = parts[0]
        vector = np.array(parts[1:], dtype='float32')
        glove_embeddings[word] = vector

print(f"GloVe vectors loaded: {len(glove_embeddings)} words")

# Make an embedding matrix for our vocabulary
embedding_matrix = np.zeros((VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM))
found = 0
not_found = 0

for word, idx in word_index.items():
    if idx >= VOCAB_SIZE:
        continue
    vec = glove_embeddings.get(word)
    if vec is not None:
        embedding_matrix[idx] = vec
        found += 1
    else:
        not_found += 1

print(f"Words found in GloVe: {found}")
print(f"Words NOT found: {not_found}")
print(f"Coverage: {found/(found+not_found)*100:.1f}%")

Part 2 — RNN Architecture Comparison¶

Define a helper function to build different RNN model types¶

In [15]:
def build_rnn_model(rnn_type='LSTM', num_layers=1, bidirectional=False,
                    units=64, use_glove=True):
    model = models.Sequential()

    if use_glove:
        model.add(layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM,
                                   weights=[embedding_matrix],
                                   trainable=False))
    else:
        model.add(layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM))

    rnn_map = {
        'SimpleRNN': layers.SimpleRNN,
        'LSTM': layers.LSTM,
        'GRU': layers.GRU
    }
    RNNLayer = rnn_map[rnn_type]

    for i in range(num_layers):
        return_seq = (i < num_layers - 1)
        rnn = RNNLayer(units, return_sequences=return_seq,
                       dropout=0.2, recurrent_dropout=0.2)
        if bidirectional:
            model.add(layers.Bidirectional(rnn))
        else:
            model.add(rnn)

    model.add(layers.Dense(32, activation='relu'))
    model.add(layers.Dropout(0.3))
    model.add(layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid'))

    model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
    return model

print("Model builder ready!")

Model builder ready!

Train 7 RNN models: SimpleRNN, LSTM, GRU (single/multi-layer, uni/bidirectional)¶

In [16]:
EPOCHS = 5
BATCH_SIZE = 64

model_configs = [
    {'name': 'SimpleRNN (1-layer)',  'rnn_type': 'SimpleRNN', 'num_layers': 1, 'bidirectional': False},
    {'name': 'LSTM (1-layer)',       'rnn_type': 'LSTM',      'num_layers': 1, 'bidirectional': False},
    {'name': 'GRU (1-layer)',        'rnn_type': 'GRU',       'num_layers': 1, 'bidirectional': False},
    {'name': 'LSTM (2-layer)',       'rnn_type': 'LSTM',      'num_layers': 2, 'bidirectional': False},
    {'name': 'GRU (2-layer)',        'rnn_type': 'GRU',       'num_layers': 2, 'bidirectional': False},
    {'name': 'Bi-LSTM (1-layer)',    'rnn_type': 'LSTM',      'num_layers': 1, 'bidirectional': True},
    {'name': 'Bi-GRU (1-layer)',     'rnn_type': 'GRU',       'num_layers': 1, 'bidirectional': True},
]

all_histories = {}
all_results = []

for config in model_configs:
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"Training: {config['name']}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    model = build_rnn_model(
        rnn_type=config['rnn_type'],
        num_layers=config['num_layers'],
        bidirectional=config['bidirectional']
    )

    # Build the model so it knows the input shape
    model.build(input_shape=(None, MAX_LEN))
    total_params = model.count_params()
    print(f"Total parameters: {total_params:,}")

    start_time = time.time()
    history = model.fit(
        X_train_final, y_train_final,
        epochs=EPOCHS, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
        validation_data=(X_val, y_val), verbose=1
    )
    train_time = time.time() - start_time

    test_loss, test_acc = model.evaluate(X_test, test_labels, verbose=0)

    all_histories[config['name']] = history.history
    all_results.append({
        'Model': config['name'],
        'Train Acc': f"{history.history['accuracy'][-1]:.4f}",
        'Val Acc': f"{history.history['val_accuracy'][-1]:.4f}",
        'Test Acc': f"{test_acc:.4f}",
        'Test Loss': f"{test_loss:.4f}",
        'Params': f"{total_params:,}",
        'Time (s)': f"{train_time:.1f}"
    })
    print(f"Test Accuracy: {test_acc:.4f} | Time: {train_time:.1f}s")

Gradient flow study — compare gradient norms across SimpleRNN, LSTM, and GRU¶

In [22]:
print("Gradient Flow Study: SimpleRNN vs LSTM vs GRU")
print("="*60)

for rnn_type in ['SimpleRNN', 'LSTM', 'GRU']:
    model = build_rnn_model(rnn_type=rnn_type, num_layers=2, units=64)
    sample_x = X_train_final[:32]
    sample_y = y_train_final[:32].reshape(-1, 1).astype('float32')  # reshape to (32, 1)

    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        predictions = model(sample_x, training=True)
        loss = tf.keras.losses.binary_crossentropy(sample_y, predictions)

    gradients = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables)

    print(f"\n{rnn_type} gradient norms:")
    for var, grad in zip(model.trainable_variables, gradients):
        if grad is not None:
            grad_norm = tf.norm(grad).numpy()
            print(f"  {var.name:50s} | norm: {grad_norm:.6f}")

print("\n--- Key Insight ---")
print("SimpleRNN shows very small gradients in early layers (vanishing gradient).")
print("LSTM and GRU keep gradients more stable thanks to their gates.")

Part 3 — Advanced Sequence Modeling¶

Build a custom attention layer and train LSTM with attention¶

In [23]:
class AttentionLayer(layers.Layer):
    """Learns which time steps matter most."""

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super(AttentionLayer, self).__init__(**kwargs)

    def build(self, input_shape):
        self.W = self.add_weight(name='attention_weight',
                                 shape=(input_shape[-1], 1),
                                 initializer='glorot_uniform', trainable=True)
        self.b = self.add_weight(name='attention_bias',
                                 shape=(input_shape[1], 1),
                                 initializer='zeros', trainable=True)
        super(AttentionLayer, self).build(input_shape)

    def call(self, x):
        score = tf.nn.tanh(tf.matmul(x, self.W) + self.b)
        attention_weights = tf.nn.softmax(score, axis=1)
        context = x * attention_weights
        context = tf.reduce_sum(context, axis=1)
        return context


def build_attention_model(rnn_type='LSTM', use_glove=True):
    inputs = layers.Input(shape=(MAX_LEN,))

    if use_glove:
        x = layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM,
                             weights=[embedding_matrix], trainable=False)(inputs)
    else:
        x = layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM)(inputs)

    rnn_map = {'LSTM': layers.LSTM, 'GRU': layers.GRU}
    x = rnn_map[rnn_type](64, return_sequences=True, dropout=0.2, recurrent_dropout=0.2)(x)
    x = AttentionLayer()(x)
    x = layers.Dense(32, activation='relu')(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.3)(x)
    outputs = layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')(x)

    model = models.Model(inputs, outputs)
    model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
    return model


print("Training LSTM + Attention...")
attn_model = build_attention_model('LSTM', use_glove=True)
attn_model.summary()

attn_history = attn_model.fit(
    X_train_final, y_train_final,
    epochs=EPOCHS, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    validation_data=(X_val, y_val), verbose=1
)

attn_test_loss, attn_test_acc = attn_model.evaluate(X_test, test_labels, verbose=0)
print(f"\nLSTM + Attention Test Accuracy: {attn_test_acc:.4f}")

        layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM, weights=[embedding_matrix],
                         trainable=False),
        layers.LSTM(64, dropout=0.2, recurrent_dropout=0.2),
        layers.Dense(32, activation='relu'),
        layers.Dropout(0.3),
        layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
    ])
    temp_model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
    temp_model.fit(X_tr_temp, y_train_final, epochs=3, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
                   validation_data=(X_val_temp, y_val), verbose=0)
    _, test_acc = temp_model.evaluate(X_te_temp, test_labels, verbose=0)
    seq_len_results.append({'MAX_LEN': max_len_test, 'Test Acc': test_acc})
    print(f"  Test Accuracy: {test_acc:.4f}")

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
lens = [r['MAX_LEN'] for r in seq_len_results]
accs = [r['Test Acc'] for r in seq_len_results]
plt.plot(lens, accs, 'o-', linewidth=2, markersize=8, color='steelblue')
plt.xlabel('Max Sequence Length'); plt.ylabel('Test Accuracy')
plt.title('Effect of Sequence Length on Performance')
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

Seq2Seq demo using a digit reversal task¶

In [27]:
print("Seq2Seq Demo: Sequence Reversal Task")
print("="*60)

SEQ_LEN_S2S = 10
NUM_TOKENS = 12
START_TOKEN = 10
END_TOKEN = 11

def generate_reversal_data(n_samples=5000):
    encoder_input = np.random.randint(1, 10, size=(n_samples, SEQ_LEN_S2S))
    decoder_input = np.zeros((n_samples, SEQ_LEN_S2S + 1), dtype=np.int32)
    decoder_target = np.zeros((n_samples, SEQ_LEN_S2S + 1), dtype=np.int32)
    for i in range(n_samples):
        reversed_seq = encoder_input[i][::-1]
        decoder_input[i, 0] = START_TOKEN
        decoder_input[i, 1:] = reversed_seq
        decoder_target[i, :SEQ_LEN_S2S] = reversed_seq
        decoder_target[i, SEQ_LEN_S2S] = END_TOKEN
    return encoder_input, decoder_input, decoder_target

enc_input, dec_input, dec_target = generate_reversal_data(5000)
print(f"Encoder input (first 3): {enc_input[:3]}")
print(f"Decoder target (reversed): {dec_target[:3]}")

# Encoder
encoder_inputs = layers.Input(shape=(SEQ_LEN_S2S,))
enc_emb = layers.Embedding(NUM_TOKENS, 32)(encoder_inputs)
enc_lstm = layers.LSTM(64, return_state=True)
enc_outputs, state_h, state_c = enc_lstm(enc_emb)
encoder_states = [state_h, state_c]

# Decoder
decoder_inputs = layers.Input(shape=(SEQ_LEN_S2S + 1,))
dec_emb = layers.Embedding(NUM_TOKENS, 32)(decoder_inputs)
dec_lstm = layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences=True)
dec_outputs = dec_lstm(dec_emb, initial_state=encoder_states)
dec_dense = layers.Dense(NUM_TOKENS, activation='softmax')
decoder_outputs = dec_dense(dec_outputs)

seq2seq_model = models.Model([encoder_inputs, decoder_inputs], decoder_outputs)
seq2seq_model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])

print("\nTraining Seq2Seq with Teacher Forcing...")
s2s_history = seq2seq_model.fit(
    [enc_input, dec_input], dec_target,
    epochs=15, batch_size=64, validation_split=0.1, verbose=1
)

print(f"\nFinal Train Acc: {s2s_history.history['accuracy'][-1]:.4f}")
print(f"Final Val Acc: {s2s_history.history['val_accuracy'][-1]:.4f}")

# Teacher Forcing explanation
print("\n--- Teacher Forcing vs Inference ---")
print("Training: decoder gets the CORRECT previous token (faster learning)")
print("Inference: decoder uses its OWN prediction (errors can pile up)")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
axes[0].plot(s2s_history.history['accuracy'], label='Train', color='steelblue', linewidth=2)
axes[0].plot(s2s_history.history['val_accuracy'], label='Val', color='coral', linewidth=2)
axes[0].set_title('Seq2Seq Accuracy'); axes[0].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[0].set_ylabel('Accuracy')
axes[0].legend(); axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

axes[1].plot(s2s_history.history['loss'], label='Train', color='steelblue', linewidth=2)
axes[1].plot(s2s_history.history['val_loss'], label='Val', color='coral', linewidth=2)
axes[1].set_title('Seq2Seq Loss'); axes[1].set_xlabel('Epoch'); axes[1].set_ylabel('Loss')
axes[1].legend(); axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

]

        layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM, weights=[embedding_matrix],
                         trainable=False),
        layers.LSTM(64, dropout=cfg['dropout'], recurrent_dropout=cfg['rec_dropout']),
        layers.Dense(32, activation='relu'),
        layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
    hist = model.fit(X_train_final, y_train_final, epochs=EPOCHS, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
                     validation_data=(X_val, y_val), verbose=0)
    _, test_acc = model.evaluate(X_test, test_labels, verbose=0)

    dropout_histories[cfg['name']] = hist.history

                           'Val Acc': f"{hist.history['val_accuracy'][-1]:.4f}"})

print("Training with LR Schedule + Early Stopping...")

lr_model = models.Sequential([
    layers.Embedding(VOCAB_SIZE, EMBEDDING_DIM, weights=[embedding_matrix],
                     trainable=False),
    layers.LSTM(64, dropout=0.2, recurrent_dropout=0.2),
    layers.Dense(32, activation='relu'),
    layers.Dropout(0.3),
    layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])

lr_model.compile(optimizer=optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=0.001, clipnorm=1.0),
                 loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])

lr_reducer = callbacks.ReduceLROnPlateau(monitor='val_loss', factor=0.5, patience=2, verbose=1)
early_stop = callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor='val_loss', patience=3, restore_best_weights=True, verbose=1)

hist_lr = lr_model.fit(
    X_train_final, y_train_final,
    epochs=10, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    validation_data=(X_val, y_val),
    callbacks=[lr_reducer, early_stop], verbose=1
)

_, acc_lr = lr_model.evaluate(X_test, test_labels, verbose=0)
print(f"\nLR Schedule + Early Stopping Test Acc: {acc_lr:.4f}")

Part 5 — Written Analysis & Reflection¶

Written Analysis & Reflection¶

RNN vs LSTM vs GRU Performance: SimpleRNN scored only 50.75% — basically random — proving the vanishing gradient problem kills performance on long reviews. LSTM (1-layer) reached 71.98% and GRU (1-layer) got 57.29%, both much better thanks to their gating mechanisms that control what to remember or forget. Stacking helped significantly: 2-layer GRU jumped to 82.19%. The best models were bidirectional — Bi-GRU hit 84.57% and Bi-LSTM reached 83.28% — because reading reviews both forward and backward gives richer context for each word.

Attention Mechanism Effectiveness: Attention gave the biggest single improvement. LSTM alone scored 71.98%, but LSTM with attention reached 85.32% — a 13+ point gain. Without attention, the entire review gets compressed into one vector, losing key details. Attention learns to focus on sentiment-rich words like "amazing" or "terrible," making predictions both more accurate and more explainable since we can inspect which words the model weighted most.

Embedding and Sequence Length Findings: GloVe embeddings (82.22%) beat trainable embeddings (76.95%), showing pre-trained word vectors give a stronger starting point. For sequence length, MAX_LEN=100 scored 76.33% while MAX_LEN=400 dropped to 51.90%. Longer sequences add more padding and need more training time to converge — with only 3 epochs, shorter sequences performed better.

Bias and Fairness Concern: The IMDB dataset contains English reviews from a specific user group. People who use slang or non-standard English may be misclassified — for example, "sick" can mean "terrible" or "amazing" depending on background. Our preprocessing removes rare words, potentially cutting out language used by minority communities. GloVe embeddings also carry biases from Wikipedia and news data, which can make certain groups' writing harder to classify correctly.

Ethical Considerations for Deployment: Using sentiment analysis in hiring or content moderation carries real risks. A biased model could reject candidates based on writing style rather than qualifications, or over-flag posts from certain communities. Before deploying, teams should test across demographic groups, provide appeal systems for wrong decisions, and keep humans in the loop for high-stakes choices. Transparency about the model's limits is essential.
